input.task: Which catalogue link sits next to the battery-life note?

provenance: M6 spec-drift audit, finding 4. `relocation_candidates` carries `index` onto every rung it proposes — 'part of the intent, not part of the tier' — and silently drops `near`, which is intent by the same argument (specs/001: they are alternative answers to the same question). So a target that fails to locate is relocated to a rung with the proximity constraint deleted, resolves a different element, and the run reports success. This is `resolver-unknown-target-key` surviving one layer down: there, an unhonourable key was dropped by the resolver; here, an honourable one is dropped by the ladder.

triage.what_this_grades: that a recovery rung is the same request expressed differently, not a weaker request. 'Battery life' is nowhere on shop.html, so no rung can honour the proximity constraint and the run must stay a loud `locate` failure. A rung that answers an easier question than the one that failed is not recovery.
triage.watched_red: before the fix: status success, answer 'Aurora Desk Lamp' — reached by the rung {role: link, name: 'Aurora Desk Lamp'}, with `near` gone.
triage.note: the answer being coincidentally reasonable here is the point: nothing in the trace distinguishes it from the case where the dropped constraint was the only thing separating two candidates.
